source.title: [Claude hunt 2026-10-20, other markets] ES opening-range break on a close. Why it should pay: the first 30 minutes of the S&P cash session are the NYSE opening auction plus the index-arbitrage and portfolio desks working the day's institutional orders through ES; a 5-minute close outside that range shows the side whose orders were not finished in the auction, and those desks keep executing that way through the morning. Who loses: the traders who sell the top (or buy the bottom) of the opening range expecting it to hold, and late hedgers who chase the break. Prior: the Quant-Portfolio book tile orb_ES (09:30-10:00 ET range, first close beyond it, stop at the other side; lockbox 2026-06-09: 681 trades, PF 1.16) and the pipeline card es_or_long (the only ES card past stage 1).

entry.words: ES. The opening range is the high and low of 09:30-10:00 ET. The first 5-minute bar after 10:00 that closes above the high buys at its close; below the low sells. Stop at the other side of the range, target 1.5 x that distance. One trade a day, flat 15:58.

not_run: THE ENTRY WINDOW: win_break trades only inside the pass that holds the first close after 10:00 (nyam), so a break is taken on the 5-minute closes 10:05-10:50; the tile allowed a first break up to 13:00 ET. A first break after 10:55 is not traded.
THE FIRST BREAK IS THE DAY'S SIGNAL: a close that breaks one side and then the other is one trade (the first), never a reversal.
THE STOP: the other side of the 30-minute range (the structure level), floored at two ticks and 0.25 x ATR; target 1.5 x that distance from the fill.
SIZING: the tile sized by dollar risk; here 1 ES contract.
COSTS AND FILLS: the engine's own (1 tick of slippage on market and stop fills, $4 a round turn, tick replay).
FLAT: every trade is flat by 15:58 ET (13:13 on half days).
THE TEST DAYS (2025-07-01 on) ARE NOT READ by this sheet: build days only.
